items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names describe what things do (flushChunk, verifyTrailer, validateSource, getEncryptor). The package doc lays out the stream format, exported APIs have doc comments, and the closer-ordering comment in storageReadWriteCloser explains the non-obvious part. Formatting is gofmt-clean.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Config validation and the stream code live in separate files. validateSource uses required/forbidden lists per source, so there is no copy-pasted branching. Functions are short. Small nit: getEncryptor calls Validate and then LoadKey re-validates. Small deviation: it uses stdlib crypto/pbkdf2 rather than the vendored x/crypto one.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Errors are wrapped with %w and the ErrInvalidKey sentinel. The writer stores its error so Close stays idempotent. The reader rejects impossible chunk lengths, maps EOF to ErrUnexpectedEOF on truncation, and compares MACs with hmac.Equal. Size constants are named.

items.name: Interface changes limited to the specified ones
items.name_zh: 接口变更仅限题目要求
items.evidence: Only the mandated signatures changed. storage.PathGenerator keeps its signature and passes false, so backend callers still compile without edits. With no encryptor, the pipeline is still gzip -> pipe, so unencrypted output and filenames are unchanged. The fileutil and handler tests were updated.

validity_flags.basis: existing test lines changed/removed (4): fileutil/fileutil_test.go; existing test lines changed/removed (2): handler/jobhandler_test.go
